text:
support-ops: alerting — multiple hosted customers (acme, betacorp) reporting 503s starting ~08:12 UTC. error-rate spike on gateway to upstream inference. visible from last 8m. customer-facing support tickets opened.

ana: looking. early triage — upstream runner processes showing abrupt exits (exit code 139 / SIGSEGV) and nvml logs show OOM events right before crash. stack traces look like GPU kernel fault.

mike: pasting log sample:
```
[08:11:57] runner: nvml: device 0: out of memory (allocated 1328MB, requested 256MB)
[08:11:57] runner: cuda runtime error: memory allocation (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation)
[08:11:57] runner: terminating with signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
#0 0x7f2c1d2b in attn_kernel+0x1c
#1 0x7f2c2a3f in infer_loop+0x3f
```

raj: is this limited to one model or across many?

ana: concentrated on model: gpt-small-quant-v2 with context ~2048 and sustained QPS spike following a customer batch job. batch_size configured at 64 in dedicated pool. reproduces on staging when I replay concurrency + long prompts.

julia: mitigation suggestion: force-route traffic for affected customers to cpu-fallback model (gpt-small-cpu-1) and temporarily disable batching/prefetch on hosted pools. quick commands: 
```bash
# shift route for customer-account
redwoodctl routes update --customer acme --fallback gpt-small-cpu-1
# reduce batching
redwoodctl pool update --name hosted-gpu-pool --max-batch-size 8 --prefetch false
```

support-ops: doing traffic shift now for acme and betacorp. notifying CS to update tickets. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled restart of hosted-gpu-pool-23 at 08:24 UTC to drain and restart worker pool. triggered by @ana.

ana: quick repro steps for eng:
1) run load test: `wrk -t8 -c160 -d60s http://hosted.api/requests` with payload length ~2k tokens
2) set model= gpt-small-quant-v2 and batch_size=64
3) watch node `dmesg` + runner logs for nvml OOM then segfault

mike: confirmed on staging with those steps — memory spikes immediately after prefetch completes and worker tries to allocate for kv cache for multiple in-flight requests.

raj: temporary mitigation approved: rollback quantized runtime on hosted pool (flip to float exec) and add guard to reject requests >1500 tokens for this model until a fix. I'll draft the runtime patch PR.

julia: commands to rollback quant runtime for pool:
```bash
# toggle runtime exec profile
redwoodctl pool update --name hosted-gpu-pool --exec-profile float
# set token limit
redwoodctl model update --name gpt-small-quant-v2 --max-context 1500
```

support-ops: CS updated customers, offered 5% credit for downtime window, logging tickets with follow-up.

ana: follow-up actions:
- raj to open PR with kv-prefetch throttle + OOM checks (blocker)
- eng-runtime to add a health-check that marks pool unhealthy on repeated SIGSEGVs
- product + support to review routing fallbacks and default max-batch-size for quantized models
- postmortem scheduled 24h after incident close

raj: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/PR-1284 — adds prefetch byte cap and OOM early-reject. will request review.

mike: re-run load after mitigation on staging: no segfaults, error-rate back to normal. preparing snippet for postmortem with flame graphs.

support-ops: incident de-escalated at 08:46 UTC after traffic shift + pool restart. capturing notes for postmortem.

ana: root cause hypothesis: quantized attention kernel + aggressive KV-prefetch + large batch+long-context triggers an allocation path that can fail asymmetrically and produce SIGSEGV during kernel launch. fix will be in runtime (prefetch/memory guards) and model config.

julia: filing follow-up tasks in backlog and tagging eng-runtime/sre/support.

mike: thanks everyone. I'll draft the postmortem entry and link logs + repro commands.

support-ops: closing the alert but keeping monitoring thresholds tightened for next 48h. :white_check_mark:
